anomalies.observed: The output pin Y (U34.4) of SN74LVC1G07 U34 is listed on the GND net. Its input A (U34.2) is on +3V3, and its /OE (U34.1) is on /LED_EN. No other net connects to U34.4.
anomalies.expected: A buffer output should drive its own net, not ground. When /LED_EN enables U34 with A high, the output would be driven into GND, which is a short.

evidence.quote: /{slash}LED_EN : R33.2(2,passive) SW7.5(passive) U1.1(/OE,input) U18.1(/OE,input) U19.1(/OE,input) U27.1(/OE,input) U34.1(/OE,input)

anomalies.impact: Enabling U34 would drive a hard short from +3V3 through the buffer output to ground, which can damage U34. The signal it was meant to provide is also lost.

anomalies.observed: The OE pin (U7.5) of the TXS0101 level shifter that drives the WS2812B LED chain is tied to GND, which disables the device.
anomalies.expected: The TXS0101 OE pin is active-high and must be tied to VCCA (+3V3) to enable the level shifter. Tying it to GND leaves the A and B outputs in high impedance.
anomalies.impact: The CM4 GPIO13 data path to the status LED chain (D5-D7, D18-D21) is blocked, so the addressable status LEDs will not show any pattern.

anomalies.observed: The gate (Q10.1) of the N-channel MOSFET Q10 is tied to GND and its source to GND. Its drain (Q10.3) sits on Net-(D18-VSS), which is the common ground return of the WS2812B LED chain.
anomalies.expected: Q10 is the low-side switch for the LED chain ground. Its gate should be driven by a control signal so the switch can turn on. A gate tied to GND keeps the device permanently off, which leaves the LED VSS return disconnected.

evidence.quote: Net-(D18-VSS) : D18.3(VSS,power_in) D19.3(VSS,power_in) D20.3(VSS,power_in) D21.3(VSS,power_in) D5.3(VSS,power_in) D6.3(VSS,power_in) D7.3(VSS,power_in) Q10.3(D,passive)

anomalies.impact: With the gate permanently low, the WS2812B LEDs have no ground path and cannot light, even if the data path were working.
